True Statement: A group of cells that are similar in structure and/or work together to achieve a particular function forms a tissue.
False 1: A group of cells that are similar in structure and/or work together to achieve a particular function forms an organ.

True Statement: Plants are stationary or fixed; their supportive tissue generally has dead cells.
False 1: Plants are stationary or fixed; their supportive tissue generally has living cells.

True Statement: Most of the tissues in animals are living because animals move around and consume more energy.
False 1: Most of the tissues in animals are dead.

True Statement: Growth in plants is limited to certain specific regions where meristematic tissue is localised; cell growth in animals is more uniform.
False 1: Growth in plants is uniform throughout the body; cell growth in animals is limited to certain regions.

True Statement: Meristematic tissue in plants is classified as apical, lateral and intercalary based on the region where they are present.
False 1: Meristematic tissue in plants is classified into only two types: apical and lateral.

True Statement: Apical meristem is present at the growing tips of stems and roots and increases the length of the stem and root.
False 1: Lateral meristem is present at the growing tips of stems and roots and increases the length of the stem and root.

True Statement: The girth of the stem or root increases due to lateral meristem (cambium).
False 1: The girth of the stem or root increases due to apical meristem.

True Statement: Cells of meristematic tissue have dense cytoplasm, thin cellulose walls and prominent nuclei; they lack vacuoles.
False 1: Cells of meristematic tissue have dense cytoplasm, thin cellulose walls and prominent nuclei; they have large vacuoles.

True Statement: When cells lose the ability to divide and take up a permanent shape, size, and function, this process is called differentiation.
False 1: When cells lose the ability to divide and take up a permanent shape, size, and function, this process is called dedifferentiation.

True Statement: Parenchyma is the most common simple permanent tissue; it consists of relatively unspecialised cells with thin cell walls; it is a living tissue that generally stores food.
False 1: Sclerenchyma is the most common simple permanent tissue; it consists of relatively unspecialised cells with thin cell walls.

True Statement: Parenchyma is usually loosely arranged with large intercellular spaces.
False 1: Collenchyma is usually loosely arranged with large intercellular spaces.

True Statement: When parenchyma contains chlorophyll and performs photosynthesis, it is called chlorenchyma.
False 1: When parenchyma contains chlorophyll and performs photosynthesis, it is called aerenchyma.

True Statement: In aquatic plants, large air cavities are present in parenchyma to help them float; such parenchyma is called aerenchyma.
False 1: In aquatic plants, large air cavities are present in parenchyma to help them float; such parenchyma is called chlorenchyma.

True Statement: Collenchyma allows bending of various parts of a plant without breaking and provides mechanical support; it is found in leaf stalks below the epidermis.
False 1: Sclerenchyma allows bending of various parts of a plant without breaking and provides mechanical support.

True Statement: Collenchyma cells are living, elongated and irregularly thickened at the corners with very little intercellular space.
False 1: Sclerenchyma cells are living, elongated and irregularly thickened at the corners with very little intercellular space.

True Statement: Sclerenchyma makes the plant hard and stiff; its cells are dead, long and narrow with walls thickened due to lignin.
False 1: Collenchyma makes the plant hard and stiff; its cells are dead, long and narrow with walls thickened due to lignin.

True Statement: The husk of a coconut is made of sclerenchymatous tissue.
False 1: The husk of a coconut is made of parenchymatous tissue.

True Statement: Sclerenchyma is present in stems, around vascular bundles, in the veins of leaves and in the hard covering of seeds and nuts; it provides strength to plant parts.
False 1: Collenchyma is present in stems, around vascular bundles, in the veins of leaves and in the hard covering of seeds and nuts.

True Statement: Epidermis is the outermost layer of cells and is usually made of a single layer of cells.
False 1: Epidermis is the outermost layer of cells and is usually made of multiple layers of cells.

True Statement: Epidermal cells on aerial parts of plants often secrete a waxy, water-resistant layer on their outer surface to protect against loss of water, mechanical injury and invasion by parasitic fungi.
False 1: Epidermal cells on aerial parts of plants often secrete a mucilaginous layer on their outer surface to protect against loss of water, mechanical injury and invasion by parasitic fungi.

True Statement: Stomata are small pores in the epidermis of the leaf and are enclosed by two kidney-shaped cells called guard cells.
False 1: Stomata are small pores in the epidermis of the leaf and are enclosed by two kidney-shaped cells called epidermal cells.

True Statement: Stomata are necessary for exchanging gases with the atmosphere; transpiration (loss of water in the form of water vapour) also takes place through stomata.
False 1: Stomata are necessary for exchanging gases with the atmosphere; transpiration does not take place through stomata.

True Statement: Epidermal cells of the roots bear long hair-like parts that greatly increase the total absorptive surface area.
False 1: Epidermal cells of the stem bear long hair-like parts that greatly increase the total absorptive surface area.

True Statement: As plants grow older, a strip of secondary meristem located in the cortex forms layers of cells which constitute the cork.
False 1: As plants grow older, a strip of secondary meristem located in the epidermis forms layers of cells which constitute the cork.

True Statement: Cells of cork are dead and compactly arranged without intercellular spaces; they have a substance called suberin in their walls that makes them impervious to gases and water.
False 1: Cells of cork are living and compactly arranged without intercellular spaces.
False 2: Cells of sclerenchyma have suberin in their walls that makes them impervious to gases and water.

True Statement: Complex tissues are made of more than one type of cells; xylem and phloem are examples of complex tissues and constitute a vascular bundle.
False 1: Simple tissues are made of more than one type of cells; xylem and phloem are examples of simple tissues.

True Statement: Xylem consists of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.
False 1: Phloem consists of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma and xylem fibres.

True Statement: Tracheids and vessels are tubular structures that transport water and minerals vertically.
False 1: Sieve tubes are tubular structures that transport water and minerals vertically.

True Statement: Xylem parenchyma stores food; xylem fibres are mainly supportive in function.
False 1: Xylem fibres store food; xylem parenchyma is mainly supportive in function.

True Statement: Phloem is made up of five types of cells: sieve cells, sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres and phloem parenchyma.
False 1: Phloem is made up of four types of cells: sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibres and phloem parenchyma.

True Statement: Phloem transports food from leaves to other parts of the plant.
False 1: Xylem transports food from leaves to other parts of the plant.

True Statement: Except phloem fibres, all other phloem cells are living cells.
False 1: Except xylem parenchyma, all other xylem cells are living cells.

True Statement: The covering or protective tissues in the animal body are epithelial tissues; epithelium covers most organs and cavities within the body.
False 1: The covering or protective tissues in the animal body are connective tissues; connective tissue covers most organs and cavities within the body.

True Statement: Epithelial tissue cells are tightly packed and form a continuous sheet with almost no intercellular spaces.
False 1: Connective tissue cells are tightly packed and form a continuous sheet with almost no intercellular spaces.

True Statement: Simple squamous epithelial cells are extremely thin and flat; the oesophagus and the lining of the mouth are covered with squamous epithelium.
False 1: Columnar epithelial cells are extremely thin and flat; the oesophagus and the lining of the mouth are covered with columnar epithelium.

True Statement: Skin epithelial cells are arranged in many layers (stratified squamous epithelium) to prevent wear and tear.
False 1: Skin epithelial cells form a single layer (simple squamous epithelium) to prevent wear and tear.

True Statement: Columnar (pillar-like) epithelium with tall epithelial cells is found in the inner lining of the intestine and facilitates movement across the epithelial barrier.
False 1: Cuboidal epithelium with tall cells is found in the inner lining of the intestine and facilitates movement across the epithelial barrier.

True Statement: In the respiratory tract, the columnar epithelial tissue also has cilia – hair-like projections – that push mucus forward to clear it; this is called ciliated columnar epithelium.
False 1: In the respiratory tract, the squamous epithelial tissue also has cilia that push mucus forward to clear it.

True Statement: Cuboidal epithelium (with cube-shaped cells) forms the lining of kidney tubules and ducts of salivary glands, where it provides mechanical support.
False 1: Columnar epithelium forms the lining of kidney tubules and ducts of salivary glands, where it provides mechanical support.

True Statement: Blood is a type of connective tissue with a fluid (liquid) matrix called plasma.
False 1: Blood is a type of epithelial tissue with a fluid matrix called plasma.

True Statement: The cells of connective tissue are loosely spaced and embedded in an intercellular matrix.
False 1: The cells of epithelial tissue are loosely spaced and embedded in an intercellular matrix.

True Statement: Plasma contains proteins, salts and hormones; blood transports gases, digested food, hormones and waste materials to different parts of the body.
False 1: Plasma contains only water and inorganic salts; blood transports only gases and water to different parts of the body.

True Statement: Red blood corpuscles (RBCs), white blood corpuscles (WBCs) and platelets are suspended in plasma.
False 1: Red blood corpuscles (RBCs), white blood corpuscles (WBCs) and platelets are suspended in lymph.

True Statement: Bone is a strong and non-flexible connective tissue; bone cells are embedded in a hard matrix composed of calcium and phosphorus compounds.
False 1: Cartilage is a strong and non-flexible connective tissue; cartilage cells are embedded in a hard matrix composed of calcium and phosphorus compounds.

True Statement: Ligaments connect bones with bones; they are very elastic with considerable strength and contain very little matrix.
False 1: Tendons connect bones with bones; they are very elastic with considerable strength and contain very little matrix.

True Statement: Tendons connect muscles to bones; they are fibrous tissue with great strength but limited flexibility.
False 1: Ligaments connect muscles to bones; they are fibrous tissue with great strength but limited flexibility.

True Statement: Cartilage has widely spaced cells with a solid matrix composed of proteins and sugars; it smoothens bone surfaces at joints and is present in the nose, ear, trachea and larynx.
False 1: Bone has widely spaced cells with a solid matrix composed of proteins and sugars; it smoothens bone surfaces at joints.

True Statement: Areolar connective tissue is found between the skin and muscles, around blood vessels and nerves and in the bone marrow; it fills space inside organs and helps in repair of tissues.
False 1: Adipose tissue is found between the skin and muscles, around blood vessels and nerves and in the bone marrow; it fills space inside organs and helps in repair of tissues.

True Statement: Fat-storing adipose tissue is found below the skin and between internal organs; storage of fats also lets it act as an insulator.
False 1: Areolar connective tissue is found below the skin and between internal organs; storage of fats lets it act as an insulator.

True Statement: Muscular tissue consists of elongated cells (muscle fibres) and is responsible for movement in our body.
False 1: Nervous tissue consists of elongated cells (muscle fibres) and is responsible for movement in our body.

True Statement: Muscles contain special proteins called contractile proteins, which contract and relax to cause movement.
False 1: Muscles contain special proteins called structural proteins, which contract and relax to cause movement.

True Statement: Striated (skeletal) muscles are mostly attached to bones; their cells are long, cylindrical, unbranched and multinucleate (having many nuclei).
False 1: Smooth muscles are mostly attached to bones; their cells show alternate light and dark bands when stained.
False 2: Striated muscles are long, cylindrical, unbranched and uninucleate (having a single nucleus).

True Statement: Smooth (unstriated) involuntary muscles control movements like food movement in the alimentary canal; their cells are spindle-shaped and uninucleate.
False 1: Striated muscles control movements like food movement in the alimentary canal; their cells are spindle-shaped and uninucleate.

True Statement: Smooth muscles are found in the iris of the eye, in ureters and in the bronchi of the lungs.
False 1: Striated muscles are found in the iris of the eye, in ureters and in the bronchi of the lungs.

True Statement: Cardiac muscles are involuntary muscles that show rhythmic contraction and relaxation throughout life; heart muscle cells are cylindrical, branched and uninucleate.
False 1: Smooth muscles show rhythmic contraction and relaxation throughout life; smooth muscle cells are cylindrical, branched and uninucleate.
False 2: Cardiac muscle cells are cylindrical, unbranched and multinucleate.

True Statement: The brain, spinal cord and nerves are all composed of nervous tissue.
False 1: The brain, spinal cord and nerves are all composed of muscular tissue.

True Statement: Each neuron usually has a single long part called the axon, and many short branched parts called dendrites.
False 1: Each neuron usually has a single long part called the dendrite, and many short branched parts called axons.

True Statement: The signal that passes along the nerve fibre is called a nerve impulse.
False 1: The signal that passes along the nerve fibre is called a nerve cell.

True Statement: Many nerve fibres bound together by connective tissue make up a nerve.
False 1: Many nerve fibres bound together by epithelial tissue make up a nerve.
